The cluster label 'C2' in Kurmangaliyev 2020 directly names the centrifugal neuron C2 of Fischbach and Dittrich (1989). FBbt:00003743 carries the label 'centrifugal neuron C2' and its definition precisely matches the working definition: GABAergic optic-lobe columnar neuron, medulla arborisations in M1/M5-M6/M8/M10, restricted lamina arborisations, reciprocal connection to L1, presynaptic to L2/L5/Mi1, one per optic column. The first OLS search returned this term as the top hit with no ambiguity. The term is not obsolete.

The cluster label 'C3' is the canonical Fischbach and Dittrich (1989) anatomical name for this centrifugal columnar neuron, identical to the FBbt term label. The FBbt definition for FBbt:00003744 covers every defining feature of this cluster: medulla arborisations in layers M1-2, M5, M9-10; restricted lamina arborisations with both pre- and postsynapses; strong presynaptic output to L2 and T1 in medulla M2; strong postsynaptic input from L1; GABAergic neurotransmitter identity; and unicolumnar organisation (one cell per optic column). The term is not obsolete. No FBbt subtypes of C3 exist, so no more specific term is available or needed.

The cluster label 'Dm1' denotes the canonical optic-lobe cell type that FBbt records as 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm1' (FBbt:00003768). Every diagnostic feature aligns: soma in the anterior region of the medulla cortex cell body rind, moderately broad wide-field arbor with bouton-like terminals at the M1/M2 boundary (~20-30 overlapping columns), shared sublayer identity with Dm18, and glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity. The cluster class (N=neuron) and region (optic lobe medulla) are consistent. FBbt:00003768 is not obsolete and there are no Dm1-specific subtype terms that would require further discrimination. The immature form (FBbt:00052305) is a distinct developmental stage term and is not appropriate for an adult atlas. The label match is direct and the definition correspondence is complete.

The cluster label 'Dm2' denotes the canonical optic-lobe cell type that FBbt records as 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm2' (FBbt:00003769). Every diagnostic feature aligns: soma in the medulla cortex cell body rind, small bushy wide-field arbor with mixed morphology in layers M3-M6B, dorsal extension into neighbouring columns in M6B, small column coverage (~2 in M6, ~1 in other layers), and cholinergic neurotransmitter identity. The cluster class (N=neuron) and region (optic lobe medulla) are consistent. FBbt:00003769 is not obsolete and has no Dm2-specific subtype terms that would require further discrimination. The label match is direct and the definition correspondence is complete.

FBbt has a specific 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm3a' term (FBbt:00052303) defined from Ozel et al. 2021, characterised by posterior-ventrally oriented dendrites and lack of bi expression. However, the Kurmangaliyev 2020 atlas (which predates Ozel 2021) defines its Dm3a/Dm3b split purely by transcriptomic markers not detailed in the report, and the mapping notes explicitly flag that the a/b subtype naming here is dataset-specific and may not correspond to FBbt's connectome-derived Dm3 subtypes. Without verified correspondence of the Kurmangaliyev Dm3a markers to the Ozel 2021 dendrite-orientation and bi-expression criteria, forcing an exact match to FBbt:00052303 risks a false assignment. A broad match to the parent Dm3 term (FBbt:00003770) is the honest classification: the cluster unambiguously IS a Dm3 neuron (distal medulla, amacrine, layers M2/M3, multicolumnar), but subtype identity requires cross-reference verification.

justification: FBbt does contain a 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm3b' (FBbt:00052304), but that subtype is defined by connectome-derived criteria from Ozel et al. 2021: posterior-dorsally oriented dendrites and expression of the transcription factor bi. The atlas cluster Dm3b is a transcriptomic subtype distinguished by mutually exclusive marker expression in Kurmangaliyev 2020; the report does not specify which markers define Dm3b vs Dm3a. Because the basis for the a/b split in the atlas may not be identical to the a/b split in FBbt (which is connectome-derived from a different study), an exact match to FBbt:00052304 cannot be confirmed. The parent term FBbt:00003770 (distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm3) is the safe broad match: the cluster IS-A Dm3 neuron, with subtype-level resolution that FBbt:00003770 does not capture. If subsequent analysis confirms the atlas Dm3b discriminating markers include bi (or posterior-dorsal dendrite orientation), the match could be upgraded to exact match against FBbt:00052304.

justification: The cluster label 'Dm4' denotes the canonical optic-lobe cell type that FBbt records as 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm4' (FBbt:00003771). Every diagnostic feature aligns: soma in the anterior cell body rind of the medulla cortex, main neurite into M6 bending back to arborize at the M5/M6 boundary and in M3B, mixed morphology arborizations covering approximately 21 columns with tiling, central columnar position surrounded by R7/R8 terminals, approximately 40 cells per hemisphere, and glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity. The cluster class (N=neuron) and region (optic lobe medulla) are consistent. FBbt:00003771 is not obsolete and has no Dm4-specific subtype terms that would require further discrimination. The label match is direct and the definition correspondence is complete.

FBbt:00013774 is the canonical grouping term for Dm8 confirmed current and not obsolete in the latest FBbt release. The atlas cluster is labelled at exactly this level, representing the pre-subtype-split Dm8 without resolution into Dm8a or Dm8b, precisely matching the scope of FBbt:00013774. The FBbt definition references the same glutamatergic identity (vGlut driver, RT-PCR, immunohistochemistry) and R7 connectivity described in the cluster report (Gao et al., 2008; Karuppudurai et al., 2014). The previous mapping to FBbt:00003767 (broad match, new term needed) was based on stale term IDs and is superseded by this correction.

The FBbt term FBbt:00111271 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm9' is a precise, non-obsolete term whose definition matches the cluster in every anatomical dimension: wide-field amacrine morphology, medulla layers M1 and M6A, columnar processes in M2/M5 associated with R7/R8, ~7 column coverage, ~110 neurons per hemisphere, and glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity. The cluster label 'Dm9' is the established abbreviation for this exact cell type. No distinguishing features of the cluster fall outside the FBbt definition; no features of the FBbt definition are absent from the cluster description.

The cluster label 'Dm10' denotes the canonical optic-lobe cell type that FBbt records as 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm10' (FBbt:00110135). Every diagnostic feature aligns: soma in the medulla cortex cell body rind, tri-stratified wide-field arbor in layers M1, M3B, and M5, elliptical arbor with dorsal-ventral long axis covering fewer than 10 columns, intracolumnar process position, approximately 300 neurons per hemisphere, and GABAergic neurotransmitter identity. The cluster class (N=neuron) and region (optic lobe medulla) are consistent. FBbt:00110135 is not obsolete and has no Dm10-specific subtype terms that would require further discrimination. The label match is direct and the definition correspondence is complete.

The cluster label 'Dm11' denotes the canonical optic-lobe cell type that FBbt records as 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm11' (FBbt:00111272). Every diagnostic feature aligns: soma in the dorsal medulla cortex cell body rind, primary neurite extending beyond M6A with recurrent columnar processes from M6A to M1 and into the first optic chiasm, ~9-column wide-field arbor with tiling in M6A, thin single-column processes in other layers associated with R7/R8 photoreceptors, approximately 70 cells per hemisphere, and glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity. The cluster class (N=neuron) and region (optic lobe medulla) are consistent. FBbt:00111272 is not obsolete, is the adult form (distinct from the immature FBbt:00052307), and has no Dm11-specific subtype terms requiring further discrimination. The label match is direct and the definition correspondence is complete.

The FBbt term 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm12' (FBbt:00111273) matches the cluster on every defining feature: soma in medulla cortex cell body rind, primary neurite to M6 returning to M3B, circular wide-field arbor covering 15-20 columns in peripheral intracolumnar position, glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity, and approximately 120 cells per hemisphere. The cluster label 'Dm12' is the canonical morphological type name used in the FBbt term. The term is not obsolete. No subtype splits exist in FBbt for Dm12, so no downgrade to broad match is warranted.

FBbt:00003719 is labelled 'lamina monopolar neuron L1', which is precisely the cell type described in the cluster report. The FBbt definition confirms: lamina monopolar neuron, arborization in medulla M1 and M5, postsynaptic to photoreceptors R1-6 in the lamina, output synapses to Mi1 and other ON-pathway targets — all consistent with the report's description of L1 as the principal ON-pathway interneuron. The term is not obsolete. The immature variant (FBbt:00053356) refers to a developmental precursor and is rejected as less specific to the adult scRNAseq context.

FBbt:00003720 is labelled 'lamina monopolar neuron L2', which is precisely the cell type described by the cluster label. The FBbt definition confirms every key feature: lamina monopolar neuron, arborization in medulla M2, postsynaptic to photoreceptors R1-R6 in the lamina, strong centrifugal input from C2 and C3, presynaptic output to L5/T1/Tm1/Tm2/Tm4, cholinergic neurotransmitter, electrical coupling to L1, one cell per optic column. All features are fully concordant with the cluster's established OFF-pathway anatomy. The term is not obsolete.

The cluster label 'L3' maps directly to FBbt:00003721 'lamina monopolar neuron L3'. The FBbt definition covers every key feature of the cluster: lamina location, postsynaptic input from outer photoreceptors (R1-R6), arborization terminal in medulla layer M3, presynaptic output to Mi9 and Tm20, GABAergic neurotransmitter identity, and one cell per optic column. Label, anatomy, connectivity, neurotransmitter, and columnar organisation all match. No distinguishing features of the cluster fall outside the FBbt term's definition.

FBbt:00003722 is labelled 'lamina monopolar neuron L4', precisely the cell type represented by this cluster. The FBbt definition matches all key anatomical features: proximal lamina arborization, medulla arbors in M2 and M4-M5, penetration of adjacent columns, presynaptic output to Tm2 from three converging L4 neurons, and dual cholinergic/GABAergic neurotransmitter capacity confirmed by both scRNAseq (Davis et al. 2020; cited in the FBbt note) and driver-based approaches. The term is not obsolete.

FBbt:00003725 is labelled 'lamina monopolar neuron L5', precisely the cell type represented by this cluster. The FBbt definition matches all key anatomical features: minimal lamina arborization, branched arborization in medulla M1 and M2, terminal clump in M5, reciprocal synaptic connection with L1, presynaptic output to Mi1/Mi4/Tm3a, cholinergic neurotransmitter identity (Davis et al. 2020, also cited by the FBbt term), and one cell per optic column. The term is not obsolete.

FBbt:00003874 is labelled 'lobula columnar neuron LC4' and its definition matches the cluster in every key feature: cell body in the lateral cell body rind, dendrites in lobula layers 2 and 4, arbors spanning approximately 40 columns with overlap, axon projecting to a PVLP optic glomerulus medial to LC12 and ventral to LPLC2/LPLC1, approximately 66 cells per lobe, and the same dual glutamate/acetylcholine neurotransmitter debate. The cluster label 'LC4' is the established anatomical name for this exact cell type. The term is not obsolete. No FBbt subtypes of LC4 exist that would require a narrower assignment.

The cluster label 'LC6' directly names the anatomical cell type 'lobula columnar neuron LC6' (FBbt:00003876). The FBbt definition matches all key features of the cluster: lobula layers 4/5B dendritic input, anterior optic tract projection, optic glomerulus in the dorsolateral PVLP, approximately 60 cells per hemisphere, and cholinergic neurotransmitter identity. The term is current (not obsolete) and is the most specific FBbt term for this cell type. No more-specific subtype term exists in FBbt. The LC6 glomerulus interneuron terms (FBbt:00049986 and subtypes) were noted but are downstream postsynaptic interneurons, not the LC6 neuron itself.

The cluster label 'LC10a' is the canonical anatomical name for this well-characterised lobula columnar visual projection neuron subtype. FBbt:00111747 'lobula columnar neuron LC10a' matches on all key features: lobula layers 3, 4, 5B with presynaptic sites in layer 3; cholinergic neurotransmitter identity; AOTU projection (via parent FBbt:00110933 LC10A, medial zone); object-detection function modulated by social context. The cluster is not further subdivided beyond the fruitless-expressing subpopulation (FBbt:00048234), which is more specific than the scRNAseq cluster and correctly placed in other_candidates. No subtype ambiguity at the LC10a level exists.

The FBbt term 'lobula columnar neuron LC10b' (FBbt:00111745) corresponds precisely to the cluster label 'LC10b' and its definition matches all key anatomical features of this cluster: lobula layers 4-6 dendritic arbors (densest in layer 6), presynaptic sites concentrated in layer 6 with some in layers 4 and 5A, cholinergic neurotransmitter identity, and membership in the LC10A subgroup. The label form (lowercase b) is identical between atlas and FBbt. No features described for the cluster are absent from the FBbt definition, and no additional disambiguating criteria are needed.

The FBbt term 'lobula-lobula plate columnar neuron LLPC1' (FBbt:00058227) matches the cluster label exactly and its definition aligns with all anatomical features of this cluster: lobula layer 4 and lobula plate layers 1-3 input, ipsilateral projection to the posterior lateral protocerebrum, cholinergic neurotransmitter identity, front-to-back motion sensitivity, and cell count (~100-120 per hemisphere). The term is not obsolete and is the most specific available FBbt term at exactly the right level. No discrepancies between the cluster description and the FBbt definition were identified.

FBbt:00111767 'lobula plate columnar neuron LPC1' is defined as a lobula plate columnar neuron with its main dendritic arborization in lobula plate layer 2, receiving input from T4b and T5b neurons, projecting to a small posterior PVLP glomerulus (posterior to LC4, ventral to LPLC3), and identified as cholinergic (Shinomiya et al., 2022; Davis et al., 2020). The atlas cluster 'LPC1' carries the identical canonical label and is assigned to this morphological cell type. The FBbt label is the canonical anatomical name (not a driver alias), the term is not obsolete, and every anatomical feature in the FBbt definition (lobula plate layer 2 dendrites, T4b/T5b presynaptic input, PVLP glomerulus projection, cholinergic transmitter) is consistent with the cluster annotation. The match is therefore exact.

FBbt:00111762 is named 'lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC1', which is the canonical anatomical name for this cluster. The FBbt definition agrees with every defining feature of the cluster: lobula plate innervation across all layers (sparser in layer 1), lobula dendrites in layers 2-5B, dorsal lateral cell body rind position, approximately 25-column wide-field arbors, projection to the posterior PVLP optic glomerulus at the PLP boundary, approximately 62 cells, and cholinergic neurotransmitter. There is no residual ambiguity. The cluster label 'LPLC1' is simply the abbreviated form of the FBbt label. Both flags are false because this is a confident exact match with no unconfirmed equivalence.

FBbt:00111763 'lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2' matches the cluster in every dimension: label identity, soma position (dorsal lateral cell body rind), multi-layer lobula plate dendritic geometry enabling loom detection, lobula layer 4/5B input arbors with layer-4 presynaptic sites, PVLP optic glomerulus position, cholinergic neurotransmitter, approximately 25-column wide-field span, and jump escape response output. The atlas cluster 'LPLC2' is defined by correlation with this exact morphological and functional type from Wu et al. 2016 and Klapoetke et al. 2017, which are the primary sources cited in the FBbt definition. The term is not obsolete and is a direct subtype of 'lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC' (FBbt:00003880).

The FBbt term 'lamina intrinsic neuron Lai' (FBbt:00003746) was returned as the top hit on the first search ('lamina amacrine neuron'). Its label uses the same abbreviation Lai as the cluster. Its definition matches on every anatomical axis: lamina location, amacrine/intrinsic (wide-field tangential) morphology with arborizations spanning proximal and distal lamina, cell body proximal to the lamina, strong photoreceptor R1-R6 input, primary presynaptic output to T1 and epithelial glia, glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity, and approximately 210 cells per hemisphere. No discrepancy between the cluster identity and the FBbt term was identified. The term is not obsolete.

FBbt:00003741 'lamina wide-field 1 neuron' matches Lawf1 in every defining feature: it is the Lawf1 subtype (as opposed to Lawf2), has its cell body in the medulla cortex, projects via the first optic chiasm into the lamina making wide-field arborizations in the distal lamina, arborizes on the medulla surface in a field of ~20 columns, and sends linking fibers into M4 over 30-40 columns. The presynaptic partners (L3, lamina intrinsic neuron) and the cholinergic neurotransmitter identity are consistent. The cluster label 'Lawf1' is the standard abbreviation for this cell type, and the FBbt label 'lamina wide-field 1 neuron' is the full canonical form of the same name. No meaningful biological discrepancy exists between the cluster and the term.

FBbt:00110065 'lamina wide-field 2 neuron' is defined directly from Hasegawa et al. 2011 with precise quantitative morphological details (28 cartridges in lamina; approximately 120 in M1; approximately 17 in M8-M10) and putative cholinergic identity that match the established anatomy of the Lawf2 cluster. The cluster label 'Lawf2' is the conventional abbreviation for this same neuron type. The FBbt term is not obsolete and is the unique specific term for this cell type. No distinguishing features in the cluster definition fall outside the FBbt term scope.

FBbt:00111289 'lobula plate intrinsic neuron LPi3-4' is defined as an adult optic lobe interneuron with soma in the medulla cell body rind, postsynaptic dendrites in lobula plate layer 3, presynaptic terminals in layer 4, glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity, and predominant input from T4c and T5c neurons. The atlas cluster 'Lpi3.4' (label variant of LPi3-4) is the same type: named by its layer-3 input / layer-4 output connectivity and characterised by the same glutamatergic identity and T4c/T5c input profile. The label difference (dot vs hyphen separator) is a typographic convention of the atlas; the underlying biology is identical. The term is not obsolete. The note in the FBbt definition regarding the Matsliah 2024 alternative nomenclature records a synonym unrelated to layer innervation and does not affect the match.

The cluster label 'Mi1' directly names the canonical medulla intrinsic neuron Mi1, a well-characterised Drosophila optic lobe cell type. The FBbt term FBbt:00003776 ('medulla intrinsic neuron Mi1') matches on every defining feature: unicolumnar medulla intrinsic neuron, arborisations in layers M1/M5/M9-M10, L1 input, T4 output, and cholinergic neurotransmitter. The report notes Bsh as a marker, which is consistent with the same cell type. The FBbt term is not obsolete. This is a same-biology, same-anatomy mapping — the cluster label is simply the abbreviated anatomical name.

The cluster label 'Mi4' directly names the canonical medulla intrinsic neuron Mi4, a well-characterised Drosophila optic lobe cell type. FBbt:00003779 ('medulla intrinsic neuron Mi4') matches on every defining feature: narrow-field columnar medulla intrinsic neuron, arborisations in layers M1-M5/M8/M9, L5 and R8 input, and GABAergic neurotransmitter. The term is not obsolete. The cluster label is the standard abbreviated anatomical name; there is no ambiguity between the atlas cluster and this FBbt term.

The cluster label 'Mi9' directly names the canonical medulla intrinsic neuron Mi9, a well-characterised Drosophila optic lobe cell type. FBbt:00003784 ('medulla intrinsic neuron Mi9') matches on every defining feature: narrow-field columnar medulla intrinsic neuron, arborisations in outer layers M2-M4 and inner layers M9-M10 with bleb-type and fine terminal morphology, pre- and post-synaptic connections in both layer zones, major L3 input, and glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity. The cluster is from an adult fly atlas (Kurmangaliyev 2020) and the FBbt term describes the adult form. The immature form (FBbt:00052320) is correctly excluded. The FBbt term is not obsolete.

The FBbt term 'medulla intrinsic neuron Mi15' (FBbt:00111285) is a direct name match for the cluster and its definition covers every defining feature of the cluster: unicolumnar morphology, layer span M1-M7, first optic chiasma process with R8-selective photoreceptor input, dual cholinergic and dopaminergic neurotransmitter identity, and Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron status. The term is not obsolete. No subtype split exists in FBbt that would require a broad match. FBbt:00052318 'immature medulla intrinsic neuron Mi15' is the developmental precursor form and is not appropriate for an adult scRNAseq cluster.

No more specific term is defensible because the subtype, neuropil, morphology, and neurotransmitter are all unknown. The 'N1' label returned by the exact search matched a larval mushroom-body output neuron (FBbt:00047989), which is unrelated and was rejected. FBbt:00006007 'outer photoreceptor cell' directly encodes the R1-R6 grouping: it specifies six cells per ommatidium, rhabdomeres forming the outer trapezoid, single axons projecting into lamina cartridges, and strong presynaptic connections to L1/L2 and the lamina amacrine neuron — exactly matching the cluster's anatomy, location, and connectivity. The cluster label R1.6 is shorthand for the outer photoreceptors R1-R6 taken together; FBbt:00006007 is the canonical grouping term for this set. Individual R1-R6 FBbt terms exist (FBbt:00004213-00004223) but are more specific than the cluster, which does not resolve subtypes. No new term is needed.

FBbt:00006008 'inner photoreceptor cell' is the canonical grouping term for the R7+R8 pair: it covers any eye photoreceptor whose rhabdomere is located in the centre of the ommatidium, which is the defining anatomical feature shared by R7 and R8 and no other photoreceptors. The cluster label R7.8 is shorthand for this same inner-photoreceptor grouping. Both individual terms (FBbt:00004225 photoreceptor cell R7; FBbt:00004227 photoreceptor cell R8) are direct children of FBbt:00006008, confirming it is the correct level for a cluster that does not resolve the two subtypes. The parallel with the R1.6 -> FBbt:00006007 'outer photoreceptor cell' mapping is exact. No new term is needed.

No named identity was assigned to cluster R184 by the atlas authors; only its cell class (R) is known. The honest mapping is a broad match to the class-level FBbt term FBbt:00006009 (eye photoreceptor cell). Not a specific cell-type assignment.

FBbt:00003727 'columnar neuron T1' is defined as the intrinsic columnar optic-lobe neuron with soma in the medulla cortex, a T-shaped linking fiber from the medulla surface connecting distal medulla column arborisations in M1 and M2 with climbing fibers in the equivalent lamina column, exclusively postsynaptic lamina connections (from amacrine neurons), and strong medulla synaptic input from C3 in M2 and from L2 (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Meinertzhagen and O'Neil, 1991; Rivera-Alba et al., 2011; Takemura et al., 2008, 2013). The atlas cluster 'T1' carries the identical canonical label and is a unicolumnar neuron matched to this morphological cell type. The label is a direct anatomical name (not a driver alias), the FBbt term is not obsolete, and no feature of the cluster falls outside the FBbt definition. The match is therefore exact.

FBbt:00003728 'T2 neuron' is defined as the T neuron with soma adjacent to the medulla/lobula-plate gap, a cell body fiber along the proximal medulla surface, bifurcation at the second optic chiasm, medulla arborisations in M9/M1/M2/M5, and a broad bleb-type terminal in lobula layer 3, with cholinergic/GABAergic competence (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Shinomiya et al., 2019). The atlas cluster 'T2' carries the identical canonical label and is defined by exactly this morphological and neurochemical profile. The label is a direct anatomical name (not a driver alias), the FBbt term is not obsolete, and no distinguishing feature of the cluster falls outside the FBbt definition. The match is therefore exact.

FBbt:00003729 'T2a neuron' is defined as a T neuron with soma adjacent to the medulla/lobula-plate gap, cell body fiber along the proximal medulla surface, bifurcation in the second optic chiasm, medulla arborisations in M9 (bushy) and M1-M4 (fine, bifurcating at M5), and a wide bleb-type terminal in lobula layer 3 (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Shinomiya et al., 2019). The atlas cluster 'T2a' carries the identical canonical anatomical name and was assigned by the authors on the basis of transcriptional similarity to T2/T3, referring to the same Fischbach and Dittrich morphological series. The label is a direct anatomical name (not a driver alias), the FBbt term is not obsolete, and no feature distinguishing the cluster falls outside the FBbt definition. The match is therefore exact.

FBbt:00003730 'T3 neuron' is defined by three coincident anatomical features that also define the Kurmangaliyev 2020 cluster 'T3': (1) soma position posteriorly adjacent to the medulla--lobula plate gap; (2) bifurcating cell body fiber with one branch forming a bushy arborization in medulla layer M9; and (3) the other branch arborizing in lobula layers 2 and 3 with bleb-type and fine terminal branches. The dual glutamatergic/GABAergic neurotransmitter capacity cited in the FBbt definition (Raghu and Borst, 2011; Raghu et al., 2013) matches the cluster's known transmitter profile. FBbt:00003730 is not obsolete. No FBbt children of this term exist, so there is no more specific subtype to consider. The cluster label 'T3' is identical to the FBbt label 'T3 neuron', and definition-level anatomy aligns in full.

FBbt:00003732 'T4a neuron' matches the cluster on every defining feature: T4 subtype, lobula plate layer 1 arbor, and direction-selective ON-motion response. No discrepancy exists between the cluster description and the ontology term; the FBbt term is not obsolete. FBbt also contains finer subtypes (T4ai, T4aii; FBbt:00052241, FBbt:00052242) defined by sub-cardinal tuning directions, but the atlas does not resolve to that level, so the cluster maps at the T4a level. The parent FBbt:00003731 'T4 neuron' is rejected as too broad.

FBbt:00003733 'T4b neuron' is defined as the T4 subtype with its lobula plate arbor in layer 2 that responds to diagonal back-to-front motion (Fischbach and Dittrich 1989; Henning et al. 2022). The atlas cluster 'T4b' is defined identically: a T4 (ON-pathway) columnar optic lobe neuron whose axon terminals target lobula plate layer b (layer 2) and which encodes the corresponding cardinal direction of motion. The label, layer specificity, and directional tuning all match precisely. The FBbt term is not obsolete and is a direct subtype of T4 neuron (FBbt:00003731). FBbt further sub-divides T4b into T4bi (FBbt:00052243) and T4bii (FBbt:00052244) based on finer diagonal direction sub-tuning (downward vs upward back-to-front), but the atlas cluster 'T4b' does not resolve to that level of granularity; the cluster maps to the T4b level, not the sub-sub-types.

The cluster label 'Tm1' directly names a well-characterised anatomical cell type, and FBbt:00003789 is the canonical term for that exact type.
